Md Imam Hasan, Advocate (Appearing Virtually)—For the Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
Quamrul Huda --------- Defendant-Petitioner
vs
Mohammad Nazrul Islam Alam --------- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif, J: At the instance of the opponent in an Arbitration application filed under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 2-12-2020 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 344 of 2019 rejecting the application for dismissal of the case and thereby disposing of the case under section 12(3)(Kha) instead of section 12(3)(Ka), should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2.1 Facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that the opposite party, as applicant, filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 344 of 2019 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka under section 12(3)(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 with a prayer for appointment of one arbitrator for adjudication of dispute between the parties through arbitration process. According to the said application, the case of the applicant, in short, is that the applicant entered into an agreement dated 2-12-2015 with the opponent party for the purchase of a house, being House No. 6, Road No. 78 (34B old), Gulshan Residential Area, Police Station Banani, Dhaka, from one Mr Khaled Rahim, the real owner of the house, for a consideration of Taka 45,00,00,000 (Forty five crore) and a Toyota Crown Car. That, at the time of execution of the said agreement, the applicant paid Taka 1,00,00,000 (one crore) vide two pay orders of Prime Bank, being Pay Order 910 No. 2020696 dated 30-11-2015 and Pay Order 910 No 2020700, dated 2-12-2015, and, subsequently, paid Taka 4,00,00,000 (Four crore). Thereby, he paid in total Taka 5,00,00,000 (five crore) to the opponent party. That according to the said agreement, the opponent party was required to take necessary permission from RAJUK for transfer of the said house within 04(four) months along with three month's extended period, and upon such approval from RAJUK, the applicant was required to pay the remaining amount, being Taka 40,00,000, whereupon the opponent party was required to arrange registered saf-kabala (transfer deed) in respect of the said house in favour of the applicant. However, after taking the said amount of Taka 5,00,00,000 in total, the opponent party did not take any steps, or failed to take such steps, to arrange transfer of the said property in favour of the applicant and the applicant subsequently came to know that there were various cases, including a case for eviction of the tenant, pending in respect of the said house. 

 2.3 After registration of the said case as the aforesaid arbitration miscellaneous case and service of notice, the opponent party entered appearance and filed an application for dismissal of the said case as being not maintainable thereby denying the material allegations in the application and basically contending that the applicant had failed to pay the remaining amount of money as per the said agreement and, as such, the said house would not be transferred in favour of the applicant by executing registered saf-kabala. It was further contended by the opponent party in the said application that no legal notice was issued on behalf of the applicant and that the case was a premature one and not maintainable for want of notice under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, which was a precondition to file such application. By filing further application dated 2-12-2020, it was contended by the opponent party that the said application under section 12 was filed without taking recourse to section 5(1)(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and that the applicant intentionally jumped to section 5(1)(Kha) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and, as such, the postal receipts of the legal notice, as allegedly issued by the applicant, should be deposited before the Court. 

 2.4 In due course, the said miscellaneous case was fixed for further hearing and hearing on legal points on 2-12-2020, on which day, the said application for rejection of the said miscellaneous case was taken-up for hearing. The learned District Judge then, after hearing the parties, rejected the said application of the opponent party vide impugned order dated 2-12-2020 and by the same order appointed two arbitrators thereby allowing the said miscellaneous case upon disposing of the same thereby giving the said arbitrators opportunity to, settle the dispute by appointing an umpire, or third umpire, as Chairman of the Arbitration Tribunal. Being aggrieved by this order, the said opponent party, as petitioner, moved this Court under civil revisional jurisdiction and obtained the aforesaid Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court, vide ad-interim order dated 15-12-2020, stayed all further proceedings of the said arbitration miscellaneous case as well as the impugned order dated 2-12-2020 passed therein for a period of 06(six) months, which was extended subsequently in due course. 

 3.1 Mr Mustaque Ahmed, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, mainly submits that the arbitration miscellaneous case was originally filed by the opposite party under section 12(3)(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 for appointment of sole arbitrator or one arbitrator. However, the Court below, in a very illegal and unexpected way, passed an order under section 12(3)(Kha) of the said Act thereby appointing two arbitrators, which, according to him, is an order beyond the pleadings of the parties and, as such, should be termed as illegal order. 

 3.2 By referring to the very arbitration clause, namely Clause-9 of the said agreement dated 2-12-2015 (Annexure-1 to the application for vacating the order of stay), Mr Ahmed submits that taking steps by the parties for amicable settlement of dispute is a prerequisite condition for initiating arbitration process. This being so, he submits that the opposite party having not taken any such steps for amicable settlement of the dispute, the very arbitration miscellaneous case filed by him was not maintainable as the same was a premature one. Learned advocate further argues that since the opposite party, by issuing legal notice, has already appointed one Barrister Joynal Abedin as arbitrator on his behalf and requested the petitioner to appoint his arbitrator, the Court below committed illegality in cancelling the said appointment of the opposite party and thereby appointing a fresh arbitrator on his behalf. Therefore, according to him, the Court below not only committed illegality in rejecting application filed by this petitioner for dismissal of the arbitration miscellaneous case, it also committed illegality in appointing two arbitrators particularly when the opposite party sought appointment of one arbitrator for settlement of dispute under section 12(3)(Ka) of the said Act. In support of his such submissions, he has referred to three decisions of this Court, namely the decisions in Abut Khair vs Pubali Bank, 53 DLR (AD) 62, Ali Hussain Faraji vs Abdul Ali Pradhania, 59 DLR (AD) 147 and Shan Hosiery vs Bangladesh Jatiya Shamabaya Shilpa Samity Ltd., 54 DLR 291. 

 4.1 It appears from the very application filed under section 12(3)(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 by the opposite party before the Court below (Annexure-A) that under paragraph-10 of the said application, he has specifically mentioned that he tried to settle the dispute with the petitioner through well wishers and common friends and that a meeting took place between the parties on the initiative of those well wishers and common friends. However, when the petitioner, through viber messenger, informed the opposite party that his bank accounts were frozen by the Anti-Corruption Commission and, as such, he was unable to return or refund the money, such amicable settlement did not reach its finality. Therefore, the objection raised by the petitioner by way of application before the Court below that the arbitration miscellaneous case was a premature one, has no substance. Therefore, it cannot be said that the said arbitration miscellaneous case filed by the opposite party was a premature one. 

 4.4 As against this arbitration clause, if we see the averments in the application filed by the opposite party by which it has proposed his arbitrator by way of legal notice, it is clear that he has wanted in fact an Arbitration Tribunal consisting of three arbitrators, two by each party and one being umpire or Chairman to be appointed by the said two arbitrators. Therefore, mentioning of section 12(3)(Ka) instead of the correct provision, being section 12(3)(Kha), in the application filed by the opposite party is in fact immaterial inasmuch as that it is known to all that such applications are drafted by the lawyers and a mere mistake in mentioning the correct section, or correct prayer, in accordance with the intention of the litigants cannot be an excuse for punishing the litigants. Therefore, merely for mentioning a wrong section in the cause title, or a wrong prayer in the prayer portion of the application, it cannot be said that the hands of the Court of law are tied up by such mistakes committed by the learned advocate in drafting the application, particularly when the body of the application reveals that the intention of the party who filed the said application was different i.e. for appointment of an Arbitrator Tribunal consisting of three arbitrators and this intention of the litigant, or the applicant in this case, has been rightly identified by the Court below which is reflected in the impugned order by which the learned District Judge has appointed two arbitrators and allowed them to appoint the third arbitrator or umpire for adjudication of the dispute between the parties. Not only that, it has long been held by this Court repeatedly that mentioning of wrong section in an application, or mistake committed by the learned advocate in drafting an application, cannot be taken as a ground for punishing the litigant and such mistake or wrong mentioning of section cannot in any way deprive a litigant of his legal entitlement under the law. 

 4.5 In this regard, we have carefully examined the decisions cited by the learned advocate for the petitioner in respect of rejection of plaint as well as passing of order beyond the averments in the pleading. However, the facts and circumstances on which the said decisions were given are not at all relevant in the facts and circumstances of the present case before us and, accordingly, the said cited decisions are of no help to the petitioner. 

 4.6 In view of above, we are of the view that the Court below has committed no illegality either in rejecting the application filed by the petitioner for dismissal of the said arbitration miscellaneous case or in appointing ,two fresh arbitrators for both the parties and allowing the said two arbitrators to appoint an umpire for adjudication of the dispute between the parties through arbitration. Accordingly, the Rule issued in this civil revision should be discharged.
